Gabon textile samples

Nathalie Du Pasquier’s screen-printed cotton Gabon: jagged shapes, checkered borders, and six colorways.

Source
Art Institute of Chicago: Gabon (Panel) (1988.484.3b-g)
Creator
Nathalie Du Pasquier (designer); produced by Rainbow, Milan
Made
1982
Style
Memphis (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Loud, energetic, dense, postmodern
Evidence
Downloaded the museum’s published image (843 px wide) from the Art Institute of Chicago IIIF server to a private scratchpad and inspected it with the Read tool on 2026-09-25. No image is stored in the catalogue. The Met’s record of the same design was read; it has no online image.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Art Institute lists six samples of Gabon, designed by Nathalie Du Pasquier and produced by Rainbow, Milan, 1982; cotton twill, screen printed. The museum also holds her Zaire, Uganda, Kenya, Congo, Cameroon, and Zambia prints from the same year. AIC record.

The Met holds a full length of “Gabon” textile, 1982, cotton, 139.7 × 403.9 cm. Met record.

A 1983 Memphis leaflet by Christoph Radl labels “Gabon – 1982” among the group’s patterns. See Memphis Milano leaflet.

Observed

  • Large jagged polygons in red, blue, green, purple, and white overlap one another.
  • Thick black outlines run around the shapes, broken by small checkered segments in white, blue, and pink.
  • Zigzag and stepped edges appear throughout; no curve is visible in the main swatch.
  • Five narrower strips show the same drawing in other colorways, including orange-red, teal-brown, and blue-black.
  • The samples hang from a black header card printed “RAINBOW”.

Why it belongs

The print is dense and uses clashing colors, and its checkered outline recurs in Memphis graphics and laminates. The colorway strips show that the drawing, not a single palette, carries the identity.

Borrow

Outline flat shapes with a thick band that is itself patterned, such as a checkerboard.

Design one pattern and test it in several full-saturation colorways.
